findings.title: Array bounds error: loop condition uses <= instead of <
findings.detail: The loop iterates 'i <= findingsPerChunk.length' causing out-of-bounds access at index `length` which returns undefined, and empty arrays cause division by zero. Input: `[]` array, returns NaN; `[1,2]` sums 3+undefined (NaN)

findings.title: Median undefined on empty array
findings.detail: Empty input array returns undefined (number type violated). Input: `[]` array causes function to return undefined, breaking callers expecting number. Also doesn't handle even-length arrays correctly for true median calculation.

findings.title: Mismatched array lengths cause undefined values
findings.detail: Uses startTimes.length to iterate but reads from endTimes, causing undefined if arrays have different lengths. Input: `[100]` as startTimes and `[]` as endTimes returns empty array or NaN. Adversary could send mismatched length arrays.

findings.title: NaN bypasses score validation
findings.detail: Type annotation says number but NaN is accepted. Input: `NaN` passes through since `NaN < 0` and `NaN > 100` both evaluate to false, returning NaN instead of a valid clamped value. This breaks callers expecting bounded result.

findings.title: Median returns first element for odd-length arrays incorrectly
findings.detail: For [1, 3, 5], mid = floor(3/2) = 1, returns 3 (correct). But for even length like [1, 3], mid = 1, returns 3 not average. True median should be average of middle two elements for even-length sorted arrays.

findings.title: Off-by-one loop bounds error causes array out of range access
findings.detail: `for (let i = 0; i <= findingsPerChunk.length; i++)` iterates past valid indices, accessing `findingsPerChunk[findingsPerChunk.length]` which is undefined, causing NaN addition and crash

findings.title: Off-by-one error in averageFindingsPerChunk loop condition
findings.detail: The loop uses 'i <= findingsPerChunk.length' which accesses index out of bounds (Array indices are 0 to length-1). Also divides by length without checking for empty array, causing NaN.

findings.title: Array length mismatch vulnerability in chunkDurationsMs
findings.detail: Maps startTimes against endTimes using index i without validating both arrays have same length. If endTimes is shorter, returns undefined values.

findings.title: Empty array causes undefined return in medianReviewTimeMs
findings.detail: Empty sortedTimesMs array returns undefined instead of a valid number. Math.floor(0 / 2) = 0, accessing sortedTimesMs[0] on empty array is undefined.

findings.title: Empty array causes NaN in averageFindingsPerChunk return value
findings.detail: When findingsPerChunk is empty, the division total / 0 returns NaN. The function should handle this edge case.

findings.title: Off-by-one loop bound in averageFindingsPerChunk causes OOB access
findings.detail: Loop condition uses `i <= findingsPerChunk.length` which iterates one past the end (i === length). At index=length, findingsPerChunk[i] is undefined. Also divides by length when empty array passed causing NaN/Infinity.

findings.title: Empty array causes index out of bounds in medianReviewTimeMs
findings.detail: When sortedTimesMs is empty, mid = 0, but sortedTimesMs[0] throws RangeError: Invalid array length. Also returns undefined element for even-length arrays depending on implementation intent.

findings.title: NaN result on empty findingsPerChunk due to division by zero
findings.detail: Empty array passed causes total/0 = NaN, which corrupts downstream metrics calculations and may cause floating-point comparison failures.

findings.title: Unequal array lengths may produce incomplete results in chunkDurationsMs
findings.detail: If startTimes and endTimes have different lengths, the map function will access endTimes[i] which becomes undefined when i >= endTimes.length. Result contains negative or NaN values.

findings.title: Empty durationsMs returns meaningless summary
findings.detail: Reduction with initial 0 on empty array returns "0s total" which may not be valid business logic. Consider whether zero-duration reports should be rejected.

findings.title: Out-of-bounds array access in averageFindingsPerChunk loop
findings.detail: Loop condition uses `i <= findingsPerChunk.length` which accesses index beyond the array bounds. An input like [1,2,3] would read index 3 (undefined) on last iteration.

findings.title: Division by zero on empty array in averageFindingsPerChunk
findings.detail: Empty array [] passed returns NaN from `total / findingsPerChunk.length` since length is 0. Adversary could send empty array payload to cause silent numeric corruption.

findings.title: Mismatched array lengths in chunkDurationsMs causes undefined access
findings.detail: No validation that startTimes.length === endTimes.length. Attacker could send arrays of different lengths, causing read of undefined for mismatched indices.

findings.title: Empty array causes incorrect formatting in formatDurationSummary
findings.detail: Passing empty number[] returns '0s total' which breaks contracts expecting meaningful duration summary. Downstream logic may fail on this edge case.

findings.title: Undefined returned on empty array in medianReviewTimeMs
findings.detail: Empty sortedTimesMs[] returns undefined since Math.floor(0/2)=0 and accessing [0] of empty array. Downstream code expecting a number will break.

findings.title: Zero-weights array returns zeros instead of throwing in normalizeWeights
findings.detail: Empty weights[] or all-zeros total triggers silent return of [0,0,...]. Adversary could poison weight calculations by sending zero-total payloads.

findings.title: Index out of bounds in averageFindingsPerChunk - off-by-one loop
findings.detail: Loop uses `i <= findingsPerChunk.length` instead of `<`. When length=5, iterates i=0..6 (indices 0-5), accessing index 6 which is undefined. Returns NaN for division on empty array.

findings.title: Undefined access when arrays have different lengths
findings.detail: Maps startTimes but accesses endTimes[i] without checking if endTimes has element at index i. If arrays are unequal length, will throw TypeError for undefined.

findings.title: Undefined returned for empty array in medianReviewTimeMs
findings.detail: When sortedTimesMs is empty, mid=0 but accessing sortedTimesMs[0] returns undefined. No validation for empty input.

findings.title: NaN returned for empty weights array in normalizeWeights
findings.detail: When weights is [], total=0 triggers the map condition but returns [] instead of handling empty case. May silently return wrong shape to consumers expecting normalized proportions.

findings.title: clampScore handles negative and oversized inputs defensively
findings.detail: Function correctly returns 0 for values < 0 or > 100. No breaking issues found - this is intentional validation.

findings.title: Array bounds error - loop condition off-by-one
findings.detail: averageFindingsPerChunk uses `i <= findingsPerChunk.length` which accesses index beyond array bounds, causing undefined values to be added (NaN propagation)

findings.title: Wrong clamping logic for high scores
findings.detail: clampScore returns 0 for both score < 0 AND score > 100, should clamp to boundary values (0 or 100)

findings.title: Mismatched array length handling
findings.detail: chunkDurationsMs uses endTimes[i] without validation that endTimes is at least as long as startTimes, causes undefined propagation

findings.title: Empty array median edge case not handled
findings.detail: medianReviewTimeMs returns undefined for empty arrays (accessing sortedTimesMs[0] when array is empty)

findings.title: Even-length array median calculation bug
findings.detail: For even-length arrays, should return average of two middle elements, not just one element

findings.title: Empty array normalizeWeights returns wrong result
findings.detail: normalizeWeights handles total === 0 but empty arrays should explicitly return empty array rather than zeros

findings.title: Off-by-one loop bound causes undefined array access
findings.detail: Loop condition i <= findingsPerChunk.length allows i to equal array length, causing findingsPerChunk[i] access with undefined value when i = length. Example input: [{}, {}] (array of any values) will throw TypeError on last iteration.

findings.title: Median access crashes on empty array input
findings.detail: Accesses sortedTimesMs[mid] without checking if array has elements. mid = 0 when length is 0, causing undefined property access and NaN or TypeError.

findings.title: Array length mismatch causes undefined access in map
findings.detail: endTimes[i] accessed without bounds check. If endTimes is shorter than startTimes, this throws TypeError on indices beyond endTimes.length.

findings.title: Empty weights array passes incorrectly to normalizeWeights
findings.detail: With empty weights array, total = 0 but the map returns [] which may cause downstream issues. If upstream doesn't validate null/undefined, this crashes.

findings.title: Division by zero on empty findings array returns NaN
findings.detail: Empty array passes through to return total / 0 which is NaN instead of handling edge case. Example: [] -> returns NaN.

findings.title: clampScore silently clamps to 0 instead of erroring
findings.detail: Accepts negative numbers and returns 0. While this might be intended, an adversarial actor sending score = -9999 would still get 0 rather than validation error for malformed input.

findings.title: Off-by-one loop index causes out-of-bounds access
findings.detail: The loop uses 'i <= findingsPerChunk.length' which accesses undefined at the last iteration (index = length is out of bounds). For array [1,2,3] with length 3, i will be 0,1,2,3 — accessing [3] which doesn't exist.

findings.title: Missing length validation for endTimes array
findings.detail: chunkDurationsMs assumes startTimes and endTimes have equal length. If endTimes is shorter than startTimes, map callback at index >= endTimes.length will throw TypeError when accessing endTimes[i].

findings.title: Empty array returns 0 instead of throwing/undefined
findings.detail: medianReviewTimeMs with empty input returns sortedTimesMs[0] which is undefined, then floor(0/2) = 0. Returns 0 for empty arrays rather than handling this edge case.

findings.title: Missing NaN/Infinity validation for clampScore
findings.detail: clampScore doesn't validate for Number.NaN or Infinity. Both will pass through to return original value (NaN, Infinity) which may be unexpected.

findings.title: Off-by-one error in array loop access
findings.detail: Loop uses i <= findingsPerChunk.length instead of i < length. When array is empty, this causes undefined behavior. When array has items, accessing index at length throws out-of-bounds.

findings.title: Function crashes on empty array input
findings.detail: medianReviewTimeMs returns undefined for empty arrays because mid = 0 and sortedTimesMs[0] is accessed on length-0 array.

findings.title: clampScore incorrectly clamps high scores to 0
findings.detail: Code clamps score > 100 to 0 instead of capping at 100. An adversarial actor can send very high numeric values to manipulate metric outputs.

findings.title: clampScore rejects zero input incorrectly
findings.detail: The function returns 0 for score === 100 due to the second if condition checking > 100, but should handle exactly 100 correctly. Edge case at boundary value 100.

findings.title: chunkDurationsMs assumes matching array lengths
findings.detail: Function maps over startTimes and indexes endTimes[i] without length validation. If endTimes is shorter than startTimes, results in undefined values. If endTimes is longer, extra data ignored.

findings.title: normalizeWeights returns original weights when total is 0
findings.detail: When all weights sum to 0, function returns weights.map(() => 0). This masks data quality issues and normalizes nothing.

findings.title: divide-by-zero protection insufficient
findings.detail: Checks if total === 0 but doesn't handle floating-point edge cases where total could be very close to zero. Also masks upstream data quality issues.

findings.title: Off-by-one loop condition causes index out of bounds
findings.detail: Loop uses `i <= findingsPerChunk.length` which accesses one past-end index on every iteration, causing undefined or runtime error when i = array.length. Any non-empty array breaks this.

findings.title: Arrays of unequal length causes undefined in output
findings.detail: No length validation between startTimes and endTimes arrays. If endTimes is shorter, returns undefined for out-of-bounds indices.

findings.title: clampScore returns 0 for high valid scores instead of capping at 100
findings.detail: Code returns 0 when score > 100. Should clamp to 100 not set to 0, losing all data above 100.

findings.title: medianReviewTimeMs returns undefined on empty array
findings.detail: Math.floor(0 / 2) = 0, then accesses sortedTimesMs[0] which is undefined for empty arrays.

findings.title: medianReviewTimeMs uses wrong midpoint for even-length arrays
findings.detail: For even length array of 4 elements, mid=2 returns second-to-last instead of true median. Should use (length-1)/2 or return both middle values.

findings.title: Off-by-one loop condition causes out-of-bounds access
findings.detail: In averageFindingsPerChunk(), the loop uses `i <= findingsPerChunk.length` instead of `<`. This accesses index beyond array bounds, returning undefined. Adding undefined to total creates NaN. Empty arrays also cause division by zero (NaN).

findings.title: Mismatched array lengths in chunkDurationsMs cause undefined access
findings.detail: chunkDurationsMs() maps over startTimes but directly accesses endTimes[i]. If arrays have different lengths, this accesses undefined indices, causing out-of-bounds behavior and corrupt results.

findings.title: Empty array causes undefined return in median calculation
findings.detail: medianReviewTimeMs() returns sortedTimesMs[mid] with mid = Math.floor(length/2). Empty array gives mid=0 and sortedTimesMs[0] is undefined, returning undefined instead of handling empty case.

findings.title: NaN input to clampScore bypasses validation logic
findings.detail: clampScore() uses `score < 0` and `score > 100`. NaN comparisons always return false, so NaN passes through unchanged. This could propagate through metrics pipeline.

findings.title: Zero-length durationsMs reduces to 0s total without validation
findings.detail: formatDurationSummary() handles empty array gracefully by returning "0s total", but this hides whether data collection failed or if legitimately no reviews occurred.

findings.title: Off-by-one loop bounds error causes IndexOutOfBounds
findings.detail: Loop condition `i <= findingsPerChunk.length` accesses index at length which is undefined. Pass: `[1,2,3]` - returns undefined value added to total before dividing by 3

findings.title: Array index out of bounds when arrays have different lengths
findings.detail: Function assumes endTimes and startTimes are same length. Pass: `[{start: [1,2], end: [3]}]` - throws TypeError when i >= endTimes.length

findings.title: Empty array causes division by zero in median calculation
findings.detail: Pass: `[]` returns `undefined` when accessing `sortedTimesMs[mid]` where mid=0. Empty input breaks the function without validation.

findings.title: clampScore returns 0 for >100 instead of capping at 100
findings.detail: Pass: `score=150` incorrectly returns 0 instead of capping at 100. Logic appears inverted - second condition should return 100 not 0.

findings.title: clampScore handles non-finite numbers incorrectly
findings.detail: Pass: `Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY` passes as valid but returns 0 (correct). However, `Infinity` also should return 100. Both handled same way now - could be unintended.

findings.title: normalizeWeights division by zero with all-zero weights
findings.detail: Total === 0 check exists but returns zeros. If caller expects normalized weights summing to 1, this breaks that contract. Pass: `weights=[0,0]`

findings.title: Logic error: scores above 100 incorrectly clamped to 0
findings.detail: Code returns 0 when score > 100, but should return 100. This corrupts any score normalization that relies on upper-bound capping.

findings.title: Out of bounds array access causes undefined/NaN results
findings.detail: averageFindingsPerChunk uses i <= findingsPerChunk.length instead of i <, accessing index 'length' which is undefined, causing total += undefined each iteration. Empty arrays cause division by zero.

findings.title: Array length mismatch causes undefined values in output
findings.detail: chunkDurationsMs maps startTimes but accesses endTimes[i] without checking if i exists. If arrays differ in length, returns undefined values or crashes.

findings.title: Median index calculation incorrect for odd-length arrays
findings.detail: Uses Math.floor(length/2) which returns wrong middle index. For array [1,2,3], length=3, mid=floor(1.5)=1, returns 2 instead of element at index 1 (value 2). Correct median for odd is at floor((n-1)/2)

findings.title: Out of bounds array access causes NaN/undefined results
findings.detail: Loop condition `i <= findingsPerChunk.length` accesses index `findingsPerChunk.length` which is always out of bounds for a JavaScript array (valid indices are 0 to length-1). Returns undefined for that element, causing total += undefined which becomes NaN, and NaN / number = NaN.

findings.title: Division by zero when array is empty
findings.detail: When `findingsPerChunk.length === 0`, the function returns `0 / 0` which equals NaN. Empty array input causes math error.

findings.title: Logic error returns 0 instead of 100 for scores > 100
findings.detail: When score > 100, function returns 0 instead of returning 100 (the maximum bound). This is inverted clamp logic.

findings.title: Median calculation uses wrong index for even-length arrays
findings.detail: For even-length array [1,2,3,4], `Math.floor(4/2) = 2` returns value at index 2 (third element: 3), but true median should be average of two middle elements (2 and 3). Incorrect for even counts.

findings.title: Mismatched array lengths cause undefined values
findings.detail: Uses endTimes[i] without validating that endTimes.length >= startTimes.length. If arrays are different lengths, this produces undefined calculations.

findings.title: Normalize with total === 0 loses weight information
findings.detail: When weights sum to 0 (empty or all zeros), returns same length array with all zeros but doesn't validate if this is expected behavior. Could hide data quality issues.

findings.title: Empty duration array produces misleading summary
findings.detail: Returns '0s total' for empty durations. Adversarial actor could submit empty array to bypass metrics tracking.

findings.title: Division by zero with empty array input
findings.detail: averageFindingsPerChunk divides by findingsPerChunk.length which is 0 when empty, causing NaN/Infinity and potential crash

findings.title: Out-of-bounds array access in averageFindingsPerChunk
findings.detail: Loop uses i <= length causing findingsPerChunk[length] to access undefined when array is empty

findings.title: NaN from mismatched array lengths in chunkDurationsMs
findings.detail: If startTimes is longer than endTimes, undefined values from endTimes[i] become NaN and propagate through calculations

findings.title: Undefined returned for empty sortedTimesMs in medianReviewTimeMs
findings.detail: Returns undefined when array is empty, breaking downstream code expecting a number

findings.title: Division by zero on empty array in averageFindingsPerChunk
findings.detail: Empty number[] causes division by 0: `return total / findingsPerChunk.length` when length=0

findings.title: Off-by-one index error in averageFindingsPerChunk loop
findings.detail: Using `<=` instead of `<` accesses undefined element at `findingsPerChunk[findingsPerChunk.length]`

findings.title: clampScore returns 0 for scores > 100 instead of clamping to 100
findings.detail: Logic bug: `if (score > 100) return 0` should be `return 100`

findings.title: Returns undefined on empty array in medianReviewTimeMs
findings.detail: Empty number[] causes `sortedTimesMs[mid]` to be undefined when length=0

findings.title: Array length mismatch in chunkDurationsMs can cause undefined access
findings.detail: Assumes startTimes.length === endTimes.length; accessing `endTimes[i]` on smaller array returns undefined

findings.title: Empty weights array handling ambiguity in normalizeWeights
findings.detail: Empty weights array passes total===0 check but returns map of empty array (returns []) instead of throwing or defaulting

findings.title: Wrong median calculation for even-length arrays
findings.detail: Uses floor(length/2) as index which returns second middle element for even-length arrays instead of averaging both middle elements. This breaks mathematical correctness.

findings.title: Loop out-of-bounds access with empty array edge case
findings.detail: averageFindingsPerChunk function loops with 'i <= findingsPerChunk.length' instead of '<', accessing undefined element at index = length when array is non-empty. Division by zero when array is empty returns NaN.

findings.title: Array length mismatch causes NaN in chunkDurationsMs
findings.detail: Maps over startTimes but accesses endTimes[i]. If arrays have different lengths, returns undefined or NaN for missing elements.

findings.title: clampScore returns wrong value for scores above 100
findings.detail: Score > 100 returns 0 instead of clamped value of 100. Logic bug in upper bound handling.

findings.title: Empty array returns NaN in formatDurationSummary
findings.detail: reduce on empty array returns 0, but 's total' is still returned. This is acceptable but empty collection handling should be explicit.
